data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The condition is whether the test and the subject share a single authority for their respective validity; when they do, the test only describes the authority's self-consistency, and when they don't, the test constrains the subject by imposing an independent standard.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a second author had written the compile.py tests","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation were caught by a test in a different file","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 distribution were uniform across files rather than concentrated in compile.py","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In the poietics record, one author wrote both the guards and the tests for them in the same week. For compile.py, the guard and the test share the same file and the same authorial act, so the test cannot constrain anything beyond the author's own consistency. For the other modules, the test file is a separate artifact that the author treats as an external check, so it constrains. The 1/9 vs 4/4-6/7 distribution is the empirical trace of this shared-authority condition.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
